observed: Relative to R08 the visible timber cuts, curved arm edge bands and layer spacing are clearer; warm rafter planes and browner/gray structural timber have separate roles.
Closed264mm-deep rebated surrounds,152mm sash bones and real53mm rear half-laps replace shallow plane-aligned boxes.
Four-banded9mm actual arm easing is visible because the pierced carving skins now stop at the inset outline.

Two measured low-sky sectors cast actual shadows; same local6-face radiance probe now supplies restrained wood and metal response. Explicit prefiltering removes the earlier transient17/21-unit warnings.
Primary tree roots/endpoints retained with real curved tapered sweeps and broader closed palmate leaves. R12 corrects inherited branch-cap/leaf-rim orientation without moving vertices from R11.
remaining: Photographic fidelity remains unaccepted. Roof/rafter/window rhythms, broad header fields and capital massing are still too regular and simplified against HD05.

Some broad wood faces are still too orange/uniform, the right eave remains too black, and the sun/shadow cut remains flatter/harder than the reference. Per-surface cool sky and warm courtyard variation are not recovered GI.

Small metal end motifs still resemble paired infinity curls and lack the reference-specific dense chased carving. Several shaded small copper end faces remain too dull; the wider main rosette and post/header ribbons remain authored interpretations.
Deep sash bones, half-laps and rebated surround add real depth, but window spacing, patina and sculptural panel borders remain more schematic than HD05.
Curved branches and broader palmate leaves improve the bamboo/arrow silhouette, but canopy placement, leaf colour/translucency and clump density still differ strongly from the reference.
The inherited onigawara r12c and present sky/cloud arrangement remain unlike HD05. No new motion/Cycles frame was rendered in this round.
